indicators.note: something crumbly falls apart into bits, so the letters break up and re-form

parts.note: the cheese, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A salad with a great deal of cheese falling to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot of' reads as 'a lot of', but 'Lot' stands alone as the definition and 'of' merely links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny, the portion handed out by chance or providence.

parts.note: to face someone is to confront them
a pack is a group, as of wolves or cards

explanation.surface: Someone squaring up to a gang in order to get a beauty session.
explanation.walkthrough: FACE plus PACK; the surface pairing of confrontation with pampering hides two plain synonyms joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask of cream or clay spread over skin and left to dry is a beauty routine applied at home or salon.

parts.note: surface reading: an app or website that arranges car-pooling online
setter's reading: 'digital' means of the fingers, and hitch-hikers arrange a free ride by sticking one out at the roadside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' pretends to mean online; here it means belonging to the digits, and a hitch-hiker's raised THUMB is what arranges a shared lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitch-hikers signal passing drivers with an outstretched digit to request a free ride.

clue.text: Fish alongside boats in area with many bays

definitions.note: the clue's 'area' is singular while the answer is plural

indicators.note: things set alongside each other sit side by side, one next to another

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
an ark is a boat, as Noah's was

explanation.surface: A fishing trip along a coastline full of inlets, fish swimming beside the boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' suggests a coastline; here they are parking bays, the marked spaces for single vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots for parking vehicles are divided into many marked spaces called bays.

clue.text: Oscar moves into first-class accommodation aboard ship

parts.note: A is the top grade, as in A1

indicators.note: moving into a place means going to live inside it, so one piece ends up within another

parts.note: a flat is accommodation, an apartment
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An award winner upgrading to a luxury cabin on a cruise liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like a film star or statuette; it is only the letter O, which settles inside A FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea on a vessel means one is on the water rather than on land.

indicators.note: something affected has been changed or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone's mere presence swayed a ruling or decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Determination' could be a judge's ruling in the surface; it is the resolve kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean refusing to give up, keeping on firmly in spite of obstacles or difficulty.

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them within the home, so one piece holds another

parts.note: reined in, held back as a horse is by its reins
the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A composed host is smooth and polished while entertaining a woman guest.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside REINED; 'checked' here means restrained, not inspected.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone with polished, cultivated manners and elegant social ease.

indicators.note: coming before means placed ahead, so one piece precedes the other

parts.note: a bishop's see is his diocese
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A priest turning up in the bishop's territory ahead of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests the church service; it is only the physics symbol M.
explanation.definitionFit: To look or give the impression of being something is the verb sense shared by both.

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken out, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a council governs a town or district

explanation.surface: Guidance issued publicly by a board or authority.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNCIL and COUNSEL are pronounced the same; the one that means guidance is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is formal guidance or recommendation given to someone who must decide.

clue.text: Be naughty, stopping at 20:00, reportedly, and sparkle

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the words are heard rather than seen

parts.note: to be naughty is to sin, and stopping at 20:00 is going on till eight o'clock

explanation.surface: Misbehaving only until eight in the evening and still managing to shine.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'sin till eight' quickly and you have the answer; the C is silent, so spelling hides what the ear hears.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter or flash with bright points of light, or to be brilliantly lively and witty.

definitions.meaning: a verb: to ransack or search through and steal

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses: the verb means to search and steal, the noun is a firearm with a grooved barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransacking a place to steal, and a shoulder-fired weapon, are both meanings of the word.

clue.text: General visiting one running magazine, perhaps

parts.note: general in the sense of open to all, as in public knowledge
visiting someone is being at their place
the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: An army general dropping in on a fitness or jogging periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' wants to be a military officer; it is the adjective meaning widespread, as in 'general opinion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is one example of printed or issued material, so 'perhaps' flags the example.

parts.note: the word taken as it stands
the standard abbreviation for European
to cast is to throw or project

explanation.surface: Hopes being raised for a Brussels-funded scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but is part of the wordplay; 'project' is a verb here, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A prediction of what will happen is what one anticipates about the future.

indicators.note: a thing that is in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box
E is the electrical abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Soil discovered at the bottom of a packing box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past of 'find'; it is the present-tense verb meaning establish, as in founding a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish or bring something new into being, as one starts a school or firm.

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Grabbing extra fruit despite a ban on doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit to be bagged; it is slang for crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade with a country is a formal ban that stops goods moving.

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
the letter as it stands
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An office romance: confessing love for the manager at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' pretends to be the manager; it is the raised ornamental knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or broadcaster's room is a place of work, one example among many, hence the question mark.

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, and in a down clue that sends it upward

parts.note: 'it' is a coy word for sex, as in sex appeal
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A racy scene of exhausting phone sex.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is crossword shorthand for sex appeal or sex; turned over it becomes TI, placed on top of RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, exhausting effort wears one out, which is what makes a task strenuous.

clue.text: Supply Liberian oil for Donald Trump?

definitions.note: an example, flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bendily, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A trade deal to provide West African petroleum to a US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' pretends to be the verb to provide; it is the adverb of supple, meaning flexibly, which bends the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The property tycoon and president is famously a person worth more than a thousand million dollars.

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: Harold Pinter, the British dramatist
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A dramatist slipping away unnoticed from Bury, a town near Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, capitalised to look like a place; here it is the verb meaning put in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave or tomb, the burial of the dead.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
the standard abbreviation for second
the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A scandal in which a man and his younger son disgrace themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defile' looks like the verb to corrupt; it is the noun, a narrow gorge through mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow gorge or route between mountains that troops must march through in single file.

clue.text: Vessel blocking that road to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftward, so the letters read from right to left
something blocking a way sits across it, so the word lies within the letters that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A ship obstructing a westbound route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' pretends to be a boat blocking the road; it is a blood vessel, found backwards in the middle of 'that road'.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery carrying blood from the heart is the largest blood vessel in the body.

clue.text: I retain strange disinclination to move

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters fall into an unusual order

parts.note: two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone confessing an odd reluctance to get up and go.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder reads naturally as the start of a sentence, so the whole clue passes for a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: Physically it is resistance to change of motion; loosely, a lazy reluctance to act or stir.

indicators.note: a thing that is in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the word taken as it stands
the word taken as it stands

explanation.surface: The first phase of a project's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is also the definition: the first era of human development, when tools were made of flint.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period of flint tools was the first recognised era in humanity's technological progress.

clue.text: Summons comedian over start of routine

indicators.note: something placed over another covers it on both sides, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stand-up being called to court over the opening of his act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summons' looks like a verb but is the noun, a legal order to appear in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order, and a summons is one such legal document.
